title: ConversationTape: unified streaming adapter + deterministic replay for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce ConversationTape: a high-level Python SDK abstraction that normalizes streaming chat completions and event-based handlers into a single, testable primitive. Goals: 1) make streaming ergonomics consistent between sync/async usage, 2) enable deterministic replay for unit tests and QA, 3) provide backpressure-aware consumption and lightweight checkpoints for resume and idempotent retries, 4) expose developer-friendly hooks for telemetry and cancellation. This ticket covers API shape, implementation prototype, benchmarks, docs, and a PR for gradual rollout.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha: Initial proposal posted. Links to design doc and goals included. Flagging trade-offs: a thin adapter layer may add 5-10% memory overhead but improves developer velocity and testability.

2026-02-24 - Marco: Spike complete. Prototype implements async iterator, sync wrapper, event envelope normalization (types: TOKEN, DELTA, METADATA, DONE), and a compact tape serialization for replay. Wrote microbenchmarks vs raw stream: ~+6% memory, +2% CPU, no visible tail-latency impact for 99th percentile on local test harness.

2026-03-01 - Design Review: PM and Design feedback: prefer explicit cancellation token vs implicit generator close for clarity. Also asked to add a simple example for 'canary' customers that uses ConversationTape without changing callsites for callbacks.

2026-03-04 - Marco: Implemented cancellation token and an optional compact mode that avoids per-event heap allocations for high-throughput workloads. Added 'checkpoint(id)' API for user-controlled safe points; SDK will persist small tape slices when running in Dedicated mode (configurable).

2026-03-07 - Performance: Ran benchmarks on runtime-1.20 infra (A10G). Throughput test with 64 concurrent chat sessions: baseline (raw streaming) token/sec = 12.4k, ConversationTape compact mode = 11.8k (5% drop). With default ergonomics mode = 11.2k (10% drop). Recommendation: keep compact mode default for Dedicated, ergonomics default for Hosted trial accounts.

2026-03-09 - Security Review: Security asked about persisted tapes containing user content. Decided: tape persistence is opt-in and encrypted with customer keys when enabled; default is in-memory only. Added security_review_required = true on parent EPIC.

2026-03-11 - Code Review: PR feedback from Evelyn Chen: split large monolithic adapter into two modules (protocol_normalizer, tape_store) and add end-to-end tests that assert deterministic replay semantics under dropped event simulation. Also requested clearer docs for migration path from existing callback-based APIs.

2026-03-12 - Marco: Addressed CR feedback, wrote migration guide and examples. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/1874. Requesting review from eng-frontend and api-platform teams before merging.

Follow-ups: add a L0 integration test in CI that runs ConversationTape against the hosted sandbox and verifies resume after synthetic network interruption. Add console telemetry dashboard for 'tape_used' and 'replay_rate'.
